questions.q: How do you reach the Fabric admin portal?
options: Signing in to a separate admin.fabric.microsoft.com site
The gear icon in the top right of Fabric, then Admin portal
A link inside every lakehouse's "..." menu
Typing /admin into the workspace search bar
questions.explain: The admin portal is reached from the gear icon (top right of the Fabric interface) and then Admin portal — a separate surface from the everyday workspace view.

questions.q: What do Fabric's tenant settings control?
options: Every Fabric capability, each as its own on/off switch that can be scoped to the org or specific groups
Only the color theme of the Fabric interface
Only billing and invoicing for the tenant
Only who can log in to Fabric at all
questions.explain: Tenant settings are the master list of on/off switches covering every Fabric capability — not just one feature — each scoped to the entire organization or to specific security groups.

questions.q: What does "delegating" a tenant setting to capacity or workspace admins actually do?
options: Permanently transfers ownership of the entire tenant to that admin
Hides the setting from the tenant admin going forward
Automatically applies the setting to every future tenant setting as well
Lets those admins enable or disable that specific setting themselves, without a tenant admin in the loop every time
questions.explain: Delegation is scoped to one setting at a time: checking "Capacity admins can enable/disable" or "Workspace admins can enable/disable" lets those admins flip that specific switch themselves.

questions.q: What does the Domains page previewed in this lesson show, and when is it covered in full?
options: A list of capacities by region — covered fully in Lesson 2
A table of the tenant's domains with their admins and subdomains — covered fully in Lesson 4
It isn't covered again later in the course
A list of DNS domains the tenant owns — covered fully in Lesson 9
questions.explain: The Domains page lists every domain, its admins, subdomain count, and default-domain status. This lesson only previews it; Lesson 4 walks through creating and configuring a domain end to end.

questions.q: Why are tenant settings grouped under named categories like "Git integration" instead of one long list?
options: So an admin can find the handful of settings relevant to a rollout instead of scrolling through everything
Grouping is cosmetic only and has no practical purpose
Because each category requires a separate license
Because Fabric only allows four settings per category
questions.explain: Named categories let an admin jump to the settings relevant to what they're configuring (like a Git rollout) instead of scanning a single undifferentiated list of every Fabric capability.
